text:
STANCE: against
STATEMENT: I wrote that retry path, so let me be blunt about what 1-in-2000 means at our volume. It's not a rounding error; it's real people seeing two charges on their statements, and for a payments product that erodes trust faster than any delay clause erodes revenue. The fix requires a safe migration—I've scoped it at two weeks because compressing it risks making the retry path worse, not better. I understand the contractual penalty is real, but I've seen how support queues look after duplicate charges hit, and "the vendor shipped a known bug" is not a defensible answer to a regulator or a customer with two charges on their account. Ship the API, gate the retry path behind a feature flag if you must, but don't let live traffic hit that code unpatched. I'll help draft a two-week fix plan tonight.
TLDR: Shipping known duplicate-charge code at payments volume trades a penalty for trust damage I can't undo.

STANCE: against
STATEMENT: I carry the pager. When that 1-in-2000 fires, I'm the one who calls the customer and says, "Yes, your card was double-charged, and we shipped knowing about it." You cannot un-ring that bell. A late fee is a spreadsheet problem; a duplicate charge is a trust problem. At scale, "1 in 2000" is not an edge case—it's a queue of angry callers I answer, not a probability number. I understand the contractual pressure and I respect it, but I would rather spend Friday drafting the customer-facing apology for a delayed launch than Monday apologizing for money we knowingly let leave someone's account without asking. Fix it, ship late, accept the penalty. That is my call to make on my shift.
TLDR: I'll be the voice apologizing for knowingly-shipped duplicate charges; the human cost to me and our customers outweighs one week's penalty.

What is the approximate number of charge requests per week that currently pass through that code path, so we can convert the 1-in-2000 rate into an expected weekly count of duplicate charges?"},{"to":"a3","topic":"Prior duplicate-charge incidents and their support/regulatory handling","experience_sought":"As pager-holder, have you handled duplicate-charge tickets in v1 before? STANCE: against
STATEMENT: I don't have that number, Chair. I carry the pager; Dana wrote the retry path and would know the volume. What I do have: the last single double-charge incident generated 14 support tickets and two cancellation requests. Multiply that by however many duplicates fire weekly and you get the support and churn cost. I'll pull the exact retry-path volume from the incident dashboard tonight, but I won't guess it from memory.
TLDR: I lack the volume figure; Dana owns that data. One duplicate charge caused 14 tickets—multiply by expected weekly rate for real cost.

STANCE: against
STATEMENT: Ravi, 20 duplicates a week is about 100 minutes of refund work—operationally survivable. But you're right that "we shipped knowing" is the sentence that kills us, not the ticket queue. I hold against shipping live traffic through the broken retry path. But flag this: the chair's desk read shows the penalty assumes the customer will invoke it, and no one has asked them. Their go-live is Monday. A two-week delay may not even be needed—ask today. If they accept Friday with a retry-path feature flag, we ship on time and gate the bug. I'll have the flag-ready build by Thursday. Ravi, can you pull the exact retry-path weekly count tonight so we bring a real number to that customer conversation?
TLDR: Ship Friday but gate the retry path behind a flag; ask the customer before assuming the penalty applies.
ASK: Ravi: exact weekly retry-path charge volume from the incident dashboard tonight.

STANCE: for
STATEMENT: Dana, your flag compromise addresses my core objection. I still hold my pager note: one double charge produced 14 tickets and two cancellation requests. Even one leak through that flag is not a rounding error on my shift. I'll accept shipping Friday with the retry path gated, but only if the flag is tested under real timeout-retry traffic by Thursday evening—my shift, my sign-off. On the customer: the desk reads confirm we're debating a penalty that may not even trigger. Ask them Monday morning, not after Friday. I'll pull the weekly retry-path count tonight and share it before the flag build ships. I still can't guess whether they'll waive two weeks without their word.
TLDR: Ship Friday with gated retry path and my Thursday sign-off; ask the customer about delay before Friday, not after.
ASK: Dana: Does the flag build include automatic duplicate-detection that disables the retry path, or is rollback manual-only?

OBJECT: no
REASON: The discussion converged on a clear plan—ship Friday with the retry path gated, Ravi signs off Thursday, and we ask the customer about delay before Friday—so I don't need the volume figure to vote; the flag removes my technical exposure regardless of the rate.

VOTE: no
REASON: The motion as written ships the broken retry path to live traffic, and I've said twice I won't let production calls hit that code unpatched; I'd vote yes only if the motion explicitly includes the Thursday-tested feature flag with Ravi's sign-off that we agreed to in round 2.

VOTE: no
REASON: The motion as written still ships the broken retry path live "as planned"; I can accept a Friday ship only with the feature flag gating that path and tested under real timeout-retry traffic with my sign-off, neither of which is in this text.
